event_text: Violence erupts after the Apprentice Boys of Derry march in Derry, Northern Ireland, resulting in a three-day communal riot known as the Battle of the Bogside.
headline: Battle of the Bogside: Three Days of Violence in Derry
story: Barry and Susan perched on a lamppost, watching the Apprentice Boys of Derry march through the city streets. 'Ah, the annual parade, Susan,' Barry said, 'always a recipe for disaster. That particular brand of sectarian triumphalism tends to go down rather poorly with the local Catholic population.' Susan nodded, ruffling her feathers. 'Yes, and this year's no exception. The march has sparked a right old kerfuffle – stones, petrol bombs, the works. The Royal Ulster Constabulary's trying to keep the peace, but it's a bit of a lost cause, if you ask me.' Barry snorted. 'The Battle of the Bogside, they're calling it. Three days of rioting, over 1,000 injured, and more than 1,500 displaced. Just another day in the Troubles, eh?' Susan raised an eyebrow. 'One does wonder what the point of all this is, doesn't one? The Apprentice Boys get to march, the locals get to throw stones... and the cycle continues.'
regret_line: A tad more foresight would have been lovely, before the whole city went up in flames.
winner_line: The sectarian divide, which gained a few more miles of depth and a few more years of lifespan.
